title: New Conditions for Philosophers to Catch the Wave of Citizen Deliberation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in advance
abstract: arXiv:2609.15707v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Powerful technologies labeled ``AI''-without sufficient epistemic caution-are already reshaping political and private life, bringing both new dangers and new opportunities for citizen participation. These range from electoral and legislative engagement to the most ambitious form: political co-creation through citizens' assemblies. Large Language Models (LLMs) could support such processes through moderation, translation, facilitation, summarization, and writing assistance. But this potential remains largely unrealized. The Democratic Commons project takes a fundamentally interdisciplinary approach-from philosophy to computer science-to evaluate LLMs against five proposed democratic principles. At its core, the project is driven by the question of political bias: under what conditions can LLMs be used democratically within forms of citizen participation that are them- selves still largely experimental? translated_title: 人工智能时代哲学家提前赶上公民审议浪潮的新条件
translated_abstract: 被贴上“人工智能”标签的强大技术——在缺乏充分认识论审慎的情况下——已经在重塑政治和私人生活，为公民参与同时带来了新的危险与新的机遇。这些参与形式涵盖选举和立法参与，以及最具雄心的形式：通过公民大会实现的政治共创。大语言模型（LLMs）可以通过主持、翻译、引导、摘要和写作辅助来支持这类进程，但这一潜力在很大程度上仍未实现。Democratic Commons（民主公地）项目采取从根本上跨学科的方法——从哲学到计算机科学——依据五项拟议的民主原则来评估大语言模型。该项目的核心驱动力是政治偏见问题：在哪些条件下，大语言模型可以在本身仍在很大程度上处于实验阶段的公民参与形式中被民主地使用？
tldr: 该论文提出Democratic Commons跨学科项目，依据五项拟议的民主原则评估大语言模型，探讨在政治偏见问题下LLMs在何种条件下可以被民主地应用于公民审议与参与之中。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the interdisciplinary Democratic Commons project, which evaluates LLMs against five proposed democratic principles to determine under what conditions they can be democratically deployed in experimental forms of citizen deliberation and participation.
